children: Senate Democrats are holding a last-minute caucus meeting on Sunday evening to discuss the Clarity Act ahead of a crucial procedural vote scheduled for Tuesday.

Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer is convening the meeting as lawmakers continue trying to resolve several major disagreements surrounding the landmark cryptocurrency market structure bill, according to Politico.
The Tuesday vote is expected to determine whether the legislation can move forward to broader Senate consideration.
A group of roughly a dozen Democratic senators has spent months negotiating over the bill, but several major issues are still unresolved.

Among the lawmakers involved in the discussions are Senators Kirsten Gillibrand, Mark Warner, Ruben Gallego, Lisa Blunt Rochester, Andy Kim and Angela Alsobrooks, according to crypto commentator Chad Steingraber.
The legislation will need 60 votes to advance. Assuming all voting Republicans back the measure, at least several Democratic senators would also have to support the procedural motion.
Democrats are pushing for stricter conflict-of-interest restrictions, which remain the key obstacle so far.
The Senate Banking Committee previously advanced the legislation in May in a bipartisan 15-9 vote.
A fresh version of the roughly 630-page bill was unveiled on Thursday.
Galaxy Digital CEO Mike Novogratz said earlier on Sunday that negotiations were continuing over the weekend.
Tuesday's procedural vote would make it possible for the legislation to move toward full Senate consideration.
As reported by U.Today, Senator Cynthia Lummis has warned that failure to advance the legislation could delay comprehensive cryptocurrency market structure legislation for years.

title: Senate Democrats Hold Last-Minute Meeting Ahead of Crucial Crypto Vote
